items.title: Prerequisites
items.text:
1. Enable Custom Styling in about:config
    1. toolkit.legacyUserProfileCustomizations.stylesheets = true
  2. Clone MrOtherGuy's firefox-csshacks
    1. about:support → Profile Folder → Open Folder
    2. Right Click → Open in Terminal
    3. PowerShell: git clone https://github.com/MrOtherGuy/firefox-csshacks.git chrome
  3. Create userChrome.css
    1. PowerShell: cd chrome
    2. PowerShell: copy userChrome_example.css userChrome.css

items.title: My userChrome.css FIle
items.text:
/**
 * Lumikeiju's userChrome.css File
 *
 * @format
 */

/* Imports */

@import url(chrome/compact_proton.css);
@import url(chrome/compact_extensions_panel.css);
@import url(chrome/tabs_on_bottom_v2.css);
@import url(chrome/non_floating_sharp_tabs.css);

/* Customizations */

/* Remove placeholder text in searchbar */
#urlbar-input::placeholder,
.searchbar-textbox::placeholder {
    opacity: 0 !important;
}

/* Remove back and forward buttons */
#back-button,
#forward-button {
    display: none;
}

/* Define window minimum width */
:root:not([chromehidden~="toolbar"]) {
    min-width: 327px !important;
}

items.title: Tarralappu
items.text:
Sticky-note-themed browser interface for AI image generation through OpenRouter.

  • Website: lumikeiju.dev/tarralappu
  • Repository: github.com/lumikeiju/tarralappu

This manual covers v2.1.0: connecting OpenRouter, composing prompts, generating images, developing refinements, and managing the resulting media.

Generation can cost money

Generate, a refinement draft's Refine button, Retry, and Random send requests to OpenRouter and may incur charges. Tarralappu's local cost caps are estimates, not provider billing limits. Set a spending limit in OpenRouter if you need a provider-enforced limit.

items.title: Manual
items.text: Chapter Contents Getting started Requirements, API key, workspace, and first sketch Prompts and shared style Style Guide, Prompt Board, model comparisons, and Random Models and generation Model selection, supported settings, output formats, and generation References and markup Shared and per-sketch images, edit sources, and annotations Chains and forks Refinements, branches, retries, deletion, and cancellation Results and media Viewing, downloading, animation, descriptions, and request source Costs and budgets Estimates, reported costs, local caps, and concurrency Storage and troubleshooting Persistence, privacy, accessibility, and recovery

items.title: The workspace
items.text:
Example workspace. The lighthouse images and prompts were created for this manual; displayed prices and costs are examples.

The header contains the API key panel, session cost, Parallel setting, and theme toggle. Expand Style & References for the shared Style Guide, two reference-image slots, and session cap. Prompt Board holds reusable prompt notes. Below them, each horizontal sketch chain is locked to one image model.

Drafting and organizing content do not themselves generate images. Completed cards show the returned media; refinements continue a row, while forks create separate rows.

items.title: Important boundaries
items.text:
• Tarralappu runs in the browser and sends generation requests directly to OpenRouter. It does not have a Tarralappu application backend.
  • The model catalogue, capabilities, availability, and pricing are supplied by OpenRouter and can change. A control shown for one model or endpoint may not appear for another.
  • Boards and media are stored in the browser. Download important results separately; browser storage is not a durable backup.
  • Reference images and prompts included in a request leave the browser for the selected service. Use only material you are permitted to share.

items.title: Orcaboros
items.text:
Browser-based tool for comparing GTFS transit stops with OpenStreetMap and preparing reviewed changes for JOSM.

  • Website: lumikeiju.dev/orcaboros
  • Repository: github.com/lumikeiju/orcaboros

This manual covers the end-user workflow in Orcaboros v1.0.0: preparing inputs, configuring mappings, finding existing features, reviewing differences, and handing the result to JOSM.

Beta software and OSM contributions

Check every proposed change against the feed and current OpenStreetMap data. Confirm that each feed's licence permits contributing derived data to OSM, and follow the OSM Automated Edits Code of Conduct. An automatic match is evidence to review, not permission to upload.

items.title: Manual
items.text:
Read the chapters in order for a first session, or use them as references.

Chapter Contents Getting started Requirements, feed IDs, ZIP import, supported rows, and diagnostics Mapping profiles Stock profiles, every editor setting, tag mappings, and profile files Retrieving OSM data Overpass endpoints, basemaps, query coverage, cancellation, and limits Reviewing changes Queue categories, automatic matches, decisions, comparisons, and map linking Exporting to JOSM Partial exports, conflicts, file contents, and final inspection Sessions and troubleshooting Saving, recovery, reset, accessibility, privacy, and common problems Profile JSON reference Schema fields, rule types, applicability, and a complete example

items.title: The workspace
items.text:
Desktop overview from the Orcaboros repository, showing the application's dark theme.

The five numbered panels are Upload, Profile, Retrieve, Review, and Export. Expand a panel to return to its controls. The review workspace combines the map, queue, decision buttons, and comparison table; on narrower screens these areas stack vertically.

The progress indicator tracks resolved items, including automatic matches and OSM-only items kept unchanged. It is not a count of edits that will be uploaded. The Export panel separately reports the number of GTFS features ready for export.

items.title: Important boundaries
items.text:
• Only the ZIP's stops.txt is read. Orcaboros does not import routes, timetables, or the rest of the GTFS schedule.
  • GTFS processing happens locally in the browser. OSM retrieval and basemap loading require network access.
  • Candidates are a bounded selection of OSM nodes and platform ways, not a complete model of the transport network.
  • The comparison table is read-only. It does not expose individual tag-resolution controls.
  • Exact automatic matches can be exported even if you have not clicked Accept match. Reveal and inspect the exact queue category.
  • OSM-only items labelled removed do not produce deletions.
  • The result is a JOSM-compatible .osm file. Orcaboros does not upload to OSM, control JOSM remotely, or provide account-based/cloud session storage.

items.title: About this manual
items.text:
The documentation was checked on 2026-10-31 against the deployed v1.0.0 interface and source revision ec79d82. It adapts the project's README, mapping-profile guide, and verified application behavior.

The desktop overview is an existing project image. Other screenshots use the compact browser layout and a fictional MANUAL-DEMO feed with synthetic OSM responses. Those examples illustrate controls and states; their stops, identities, and changes must not be uploaded to OpenStreetMap.

items.title: Getting started
items.text: Orcaboros runs at lumikeiju.dev/orcaboros. Using the hosted application does not require installing Orcaboros or its development tools.

items.title: Before you begin
items.text:
Have the following ready:

  • A modern browser. The map requires WebGL2; the review queue remains available if map initialization fails.
  • One or more local GTFS ZIP files, with permission to use their data for the intended OSM contribution.
  • An appropriate HTTPS Overpass endpoint for retrieving OSM data.
  • JOSM for inspecting the exported file. Any eventual OSM upload happens there, not in Orcaboros.

Read and acknowledge the beta warning. Keep the original archives outside the application: its saved session does not retain the ZIP bytes.

items.title: Select archives and identify feeds
items.text:
1. Expand Upload.
  2. Use Choose or drop GTFS ZIPs, or drop the archives onto the upload area.
  3. Check the GTFS Feed ID beside every selected ZIP.
  4. Remove any accidentally selected archive before processing.
  5. Select Process selected GTFS ZIPs.

A feed ID defaults to the filename without .zip, trimmed and uppercased. It is not inferred from agency.txt or other feed metadata. For example, a stock King County Metro feed needs the ID US-WA-KCM, even if the downloaded archive has a different name.

Feed IDs:

  • Use letters and digits, optionally separated by single hyphens.
  • Must be unique among the selected archives.
  • Have a maximum length of 242 characters.
  • Cannot be the consolidated feed ID US-WA-PSC, which Orcaboros explicitly rejects.

See the stock feed table before importing. If even one selected feed lacks a stock profile, the application starts with a blank custom profile for all selected feeds.

items.title: Check the import result
items.text:
Fictional example: four eligible stops were imported from one source feed.

During processing, Cancel import stops the operation. An import is staged before becoming active: a failed or cancelled replacement leaves the previous active session intact. Merely selecting new ZIP files does not replace the session either.

After processing:

  1. Confirm the imported feed IDs and eligible-stop count.
  2. Read each feed's diagnostics, including skipped and unsupported-location counts.
  3. Investigate unexpected omissions before continuing. The interface shows the first five diagnostic details per feed, not necessarily every problematic row.
  4. Select Continue to profile mapping.

A successful replacement activates the newly imported session. Export any useful earlier work before deliberately replacing it.

items.title: Supported ZIP contents
items.text:
Orcaboros reads the exact ZIP-root entry stops.txt. A nested file such as feed/stops.txt is not the required entry. Other GTFS files are not processed.

The file must be valid UTF-8 CSV with these columns:

Column Requirement stop_id Nonempty, at most 255 characters, with no control characters; unique within the feed stop_name Nonempty and at most 255 characters stop_lat Finite WGS84 latitude, between -90 and 90 stop_lon Finite WGS84 longitude, between -180 and 180

Duplicate stop IDs fail that feed's import; they are not silently merged. The same stop ID in different feeds has a different source identity.

location_type determines which rows are eligible:

Value Treatment Missing, blank, or 0 Platform 1 Station Other values Skipped as unsupported

Columns such as stop_code and parent_station can be used in mappings, as can other existing CSV headers. Reading a field does not itself create an OSM tag or relationship; the profile decides what to propose.

items.title: Import failures and skipped rows
items.text:
A corrupt archive, missing or duplicate root stops.txt, invalid encoding or CSV structure, missing required columns, or duplicate stop IDs can prevent import. Invalid individual rows are otherwise skipped with diagnostics.

Check the archive and source data rather than treating a smaller eligible-stop count as a complete feed. Orcaboros retains every valid stop_id for identity checks, even when that row is skipped for invalid coordinates, another invalid value, or an unsupported location type. Such a row does not make its OSM identity appear removed. A missing or invalid stop_id cannot provide that protection.

For recovery advice, see Sessions and troubleshooting.

Next: Mapping profiles.

items.title: Mapping profiles
items.text:
A profile defines how imported stops become proposed OSM tags, which existing tags to remove, which coordinates to retain, and how far away to search for matches. Inspect it before retrieving candidates.

Profile changes invalidate review work

Applying a compatible profile change reprocesses the imported stops and clears the candidate results, reviews, and export draft. Retrieve OSM data again afterward. Export any useful work before changing mappings or radii mid-session.

items.title: Stock profiles
items.text:
The upload feed ID must match one of these IDs to select its stock profile.

Feed ID Agency US-WA-CT Community Transit US-WA-ET Everett Transit US-WA-IT Intercity Transit US-WA-KCM King County Metro US-WA-KT Kitsap Transit US-WA-PT Pierce Transit US-WA-SCM Seattle Center Monorail US-WA-ST Sound Transit US-WA-WSF Washington State Ferries

When every imported feed has a stock profile, Orcaboros combines them. Their sections initially collapse and display Auto-matched; expand each one to inspect its settings. This profile-selection label is separate from an automatically matched OSM feature.

If any feed ID is unknown, the application creates a blank custom profile for all selected feeds. It has no field mappings, additional tags, or removal keys. Configure it yourself or import a compatible profile; do not assume the other feeds kept their stock rules. Custom feed IDs are not added to the stock registry.

Stock profiles:

  • Map stop_name_expanded to name.
  • Map stop_code to gtfs:stop_code:<FEED_ID>.
  • Do not map stop_id to an output tag.
  • Propose public_transport=platform and highway=bus_stop for platform rows.
  • Propose removing gtfs:stop_id, gtfs:stop_id:<FEED_ID>, and gtfs:feed from matched elements.

These are the supplied defaults, not a guarantee that every resulting tag suits every transport mode or feature. Station rows do not receive the platform-only constants.

items.title: Matching radii
items.text:
Fictional profile with 50 m candidate and 10 m auto-match radii. More mapping rows continue below the visible area.

Setting Default Effect Candidate radius (m) 50 Controls the nearby candidate search and the retrieval padding Auto-match radius 10 Maximum distance for a unique exact-identity candidate to be automatically selected

Both values must be greater than zero and at most 10,000 m. The auto-match radius cannot exceed the candidate radius.

Increasing a radius does not make proximity reliable evidence of identity. Name similarity and distance alone never produce an automatic match; see matching behavior.

items.title: Geometry target
items.text:
Each feed has a Geometry target switch:

  • OSM, the default, preserves the selected existing OSM element's position.
  • GTFS uses the feed coordinates for matched nodes.

Platform ways retain their member geometry with either setting. Their center is used for matching, not as a replacement for the way's shape. New nodes use GTFS coordinates regardless of this switch.

Check locations against the actual stop or platform. Choosing GTFS does not establish that the feed coordinates are more accurate.

items.title: Street name cleanup
items.text:
Street name cleanup is enabled by default. It cleans all-uppercase names and expands supported US street abbreviations and directions.

The cleaned value is available as stop_name_expanded. The original stop_name remains available, so a mapping can deliberately use the raw name instead. This is name processing, not translation or a general international address-normalization service.

Review the example outputs and the final comparison, especially when working outside the stock profiles' region.

items.title: GTFS fields to OSM tags
items.text:
The GTFS fields to OSM tags table pairs an imported or computed field with an OSM key. Enter the destination key beside the field you want to use.

  • A blank OSM key means ignore this field.
  • Examples show how values from the imported feed map to the chosen key.
  • A field's presence in the CSV does not mean it should be copied into OSM.
  • Empty resolved values do not produce tags.
  • Active mappings must use valid keys and values; duplicate output keys applying to the same feature are invalid.

Useful computed fields are stop_name_expanded, source_feed_id, and source_feed_name. The JSON reference also describes feed- and location-specific rules.

items.title: Additional OSM tags
items.text:
Use Add OSM tag to add a constant key/value rule under Additional OSM tags. These rules belong to the feed section containing them.

Existing rules may instead take a value from a GTFS field or the feed's metadata. The editor identifies that source; it is not a free-text constant value. Use profile JSON for those rule types and explicit applicability restrictions.

A partially filled editor row is inactive. Complete it before expecting an output tag, or clear/remove it if it was accidental. Inactive rows are omitted from exported profile JSON.

items.title: OSM keys to remove
items.text:
Use Add OSM key to remove under OSM keys to remove to name an existing tag key that should be removed from matched elements.

  • Removal rules apply to matched OSM elements, not new nodes.
  • An active mapping for the same key takes precedence over removal.
  • Unmapped keys not selected for removal are preserved.
  • Matching legacy generic GTFS identities can also produce identity-tag removal proposals.

Feed-specific gtfs:stop_id:<FEED_ID> tags can therefore help identify a match even when the profile proposes removing them from the result. Identification and output tagging are separate operations.

The comparison defaults explain which values are retained. The current UI does not provide a separate accept/reject control for each tag removal.

items.title: Managing profile JSON
items.text:
• Export profile JSON saves the active mapping configuration for reuse. It does not back up the entire session.
  • Import profile JSON loads and validates a profile file.
  • Reset stock profile returns to the combined stock configuration, subject to compatibility with the currently imported feeds.

An imported profile must enable every imported feed. Invalid active rules or an incompatible feed selection are rejected rather than replacing the working profile.

Resetting to stock cannot supply a stock definition for an unknown custom feed. If your session includes such a feed, the reset may be rejected; use or edit a compatible custom profile instead.

When the profile is ready, select Continue to OSM retrieval.

Next: Retrieving OSM data.

items.title: Retrieving OSM data
items.text: Retrieval obtains an OSM snapshot for comparison with the imported stops. It does not edit OpenStreetMap.

items.title: Choose an endpoint
items.text:
1. Finish the mapping profile, including both matching radii.
  2. Expand Retrieve.
  3. Enter a URL in HTTPS Overpass-compatible endpoint.
  4. Optionally enter a custom basemap URL.
  5. Select Retrieve Candidates.

Use an HTTPS endpoint that supports Overpass queries and browser access. The information link beside the endpoint field leads to the OSM wiki's public Overpass instances. Follow the chosen service's usage policy.

The endpoint field masks its contents. Its value is used only for the current browser session and is not restored after a reload. A masked field does not make the remote service anonymous: the service still receives the request.

items.title: Basemap settings
items.text:
Without a custom style, the map uses OpenFreeMap:

Application theme Default basemap Dark Fiord Light Positron

Optional session-only MapLibre style URL selects a different map style. Supply a MapLibre-compatible style URL, not an ordinary map website or an Overpass endpoint.

The style and its referenced resources must be accessible to the browser. Custom styles may use their own tile providers and access policies. The style URL is not persisted and must be entered again after a reload.

Basemap features are visual context. They are not the retrieved OSM candidate snapshot, and a feature drawn in the basemap is not necessarily available to select as a match.

items.title: What is requested
items.text:
The query covers the imported stop extent, padded by the candidate radius. It requests:

  • Nodes tagged highway=bus_stop.
  • Nodes and ways tagged public_transport=platform.
  • Nodes carrying the selected feed-specific GTFS identity tags.

This is not an unrestricted search of every OSM object. Relations and other unsupported feature types are outside this workflow. Importing a station row does not imply that every possible station representation will be retrieved.

After the request, Orcaboros matches candidates locally. A lack of matching results is not proof that the stop is missing from OSM.

items.title: Progress and completion
items.text:
Fictional example using an intercepted demonstration endpoint, not a public Overpass service.

Watch the request and local-matching progress, then check the resulting candidate count. Select Continue to review when retrieval succeeds.

Cancel OSM Request stops an active request. A failed or cancelled request preserves the last successful snapshot and its reviews. A successful refresh replaces that snapshot and invalidates the previous review decisions and export draft.

Refreshing is not a merge

Retrieve again only when you intend to rebuild the candidate set and redo the review. Export useful progress first; an earlier .osm file is a separate artifact, not a session restore point.

items.title: Limits and failures
items.text:
Limit Value Requested Overpass query timeout 60 seconds Client request timeout 75 seconds Maximum response size 25 MiB Maximum elements per response 50,000

Server-side limits can be stricter. An Overpass runtime-error remark, invalid response, unsupported data, HTTP/CORS problem, timeout, or exceeded limit is a failure, not a successful empty result.

For a failed request:

  1. Read the displayed error.
  2. Check the endpoint URL and the service's availability and browser-access policy.
  3. Check whether the selected feeds cover an unexpectedly large area.
  4. Retry when appropriate, or use another suitable endpoint.

Do not repeatedly send an oversized query to a busy public instance. If you need to change the feed selection or profile, account for the resulting session/review reset.

A successful zero-result response is different from a failure. Confirm the geographic extent, feed IDs, search radius, and supported candidate types before treating any feature as new.

Next: Reviewing changes.

items.title: Reviewing changes
items.text: The review workspace connects three panes: Review Queue, Decision, and Comparison, alongside the map. Open Review, then use Open Review Queue if needed.

items.title: Matching and automatic decisions
items.text:
Candidates are ordered by:

  1. Exact feed-specific identity.
  2. Normalized, expanded-name agreement.
  3. Distance.
  4. Element ID as a tie-breaker.

An automatic match requires exactly one exact-identity candidate within the auto-match radius. Matching names or short distances alone never auto-select a candidate.

Inspect automatic matches before export

The exact category is hidden by default, but its auto-matched stops can already be included in an export. Open Filters, enable exact, and check them individually. You do not have to click Accept match for an automatic match to become exportable.

items.title: Queue categories and filters
items.text:
Categories describe the relationship to retrieved identity evidence. They do not determine what you should edit.

Category Meaning What not to assume new No exact-identity candidate was found An existing untagged or differently tagged OSM stop may still be the right match moved Exact identity exists beyond the auto-match radius The feed coordinates are not automatically more accurate exact Exact identity exists within the auto-match radius The tags, coordinates, and identity still need checking; ambiguity can prevent automatic selection removed A retrieved OSM identity is absent from all valid stop IDs in the imported feed The physical feature has not necessarily disappeared

Filters independently toggles new, removed, moved, and exact results. New, removed, and moved are enabled initially; exact is initially disabled. Changing a filter hides or reveals items but does not discard their decisions or exclude them from export.

Fictional examples show an automatic match, an accepted match, and an unreviewed stop. Category counts and decision states are separate.

The queue shows ten results per page. When more than one page is needed, use First, Previous, Next, and Last. The result range describes the filtered list; the queue's total can be larger. If nothing is shown, use Check filters? or reopen Filters before concluding that review is finished.

items.title: Make a decision
items.text:
Select a queue item or its map-focus control. Check the candidate, tags, and coordinates before using the Decision pane.

Action Result Accept match Records the selected candidate as the OSM element for this stop Skip feature Leaves the stop out of the export Create separate node Proposes a new node at the GTFS coordinates instead of modifying an existing candidate

Accept match requires a candidate. Creating a separate node is an explicit choice, not the required action for every item labelled new. Check for existing features before creating duplicates.

Decision-pane actions advance to the next visible item. You can revisit a stop and change its decision. For a different existing candidate, use the map's link controls.

The state labels record your progress:

State Export treatment unreviewed Excluded auto-matched Included without an additional acceptance click match-selected Included as a selected existing element create-selected Included as a new node skipped Excluded

These are decision states, not the new/moved/exact categories. A new-category stop can become match-selected after you identify an existing OSM feature.

items.title: Read the comparison
items.text:
Fictional moved stop. The comparison proposes a stop-code tag and shows an existing identity tag; location metadata is separate from OSM tags.

The left side shows profile-mapped GTFS tags, not every raw CSV field. The right side shows the selected OSM element's tags. Coordinates and calculated match distance appear in a separate metadata table below.

Addition and removal/replacement highlighting draws attention to differences. The table is read-only: there are no per-tag checkboxes, value editors, or accept/reject controls in this interface. Highlighting is not a promise that every differing GTFS value will overwrite OSM.

items.title: What happens to tags
items.text:
For a selected match, the default proposal behaves as follows:

Situation Default result A mapped key is missing from OSM Add the proposed value An existing OSM key has no mapping or removal rule Preserve it A mapped value differs from the existing value Normally keep the current OSM value Existing and proposed name values are equivalent after name normalization Accept the proposed name form An existing key is configured for removal Remove it unless an active mapping supplies that key

New nodes receive the profile's resolved tags and have no existing OSM tags to preserve.

If these defaults are not the desired result, either revise the profile and retrieve/review again, or make the necessary final changes in JOSM. Do not assume that clicking a highlighted comparison cell changes the export.

items.title: OSM-only items
items.text:
An item labelled removed has an identity absent from all valid stop IDs in the imported feed, not just the eligible stops. A row with a valid stop_id remains in that identity set even if its coordinates or location type prevent it from being reviewed. A feed change, omitted row, or invalid stop_id can still leave an OSM identity absent; this is not proof that the physical feature disappeared.

Inspect it, then use Keep OSM element unchanged to record that review. Orcaboros does not propose or export an element deletion. An item kept unchanged contributes to review progress, but it is not an additional edited GTFS feature in the export count.

items.title: Using the map
items.text:
Use the queue's focus controls to locate a feature. Map and queue focus are synchronized. Pan and zoom to inspect the surroundings, and open feature popups to distinguish mapped GTFS tags from existing OSM tags.

The expandable Map Legend explains match-found, moved, unmatched, removed, pending, reviewed, candidate, and connection symbols. Focused and alternative candidates have distinct indicators.

Individual feature detail appears at zoom 11 and above. At lower zooms, Zoom in to view data explains why detail is hidden; established connections remain visible. A hidden point at low zoom is not a failed import.

To link a stop to another retrieved candidate:

  1. Open the GTFS stop's popup.
  2. Select Change Link.
  3. Preview the connection and choose the intended retrieved OSM candidate.
  4. Commit the new target by selecting it on the map.

The original connection remains until a replacement is committed. Use Cancel Link or Escape to cancel without replacing it. Proximity alone does not establish a valid match, and basemap-only features are not selectable retrieved candidates.

If WebGL2 or map initialization fails, use Retry map. The review queue remains available, but do not approve uncertain geometry simply because the map is unavailable.

Next: Exporting to JOSM.

items.title: Exporting to JOSM
items.text: Orcaboros exports a JOSM-compatible .osm file. It does not upload changes to OpenStreetMap or send them to JOSM through Remote Control.

items.title: Check what will be included
items.text:
Export supports partial progress:

  • auto-matched, match-selected, and create-selected stops are eligible.
  • unreviewed and skipped stops are excluded.
  • OSM-only items kept unchanged do not produce deletions.

Queue filters affect visibility, not export eligibility. In particular, hiding the exact category does not exclude its automatic matches.

Before downloading:

  1. Reveal exact in the review filters and inspect automatic matches.
  2. Check every selected candidate and every proposed new node.
  3. Confirm geometry settings, tag additions, preserved values, and removals.
  4. Resolve conflicting decisions.
  5. Verify that the ready-to-export count agrees with the decisions you intend to include.

items.title: Download the file
items.text:
1. Expand Export.
  2. Read the number of features ready to export.
  3. Select Download JOSM OSM File.
  4. Save the downloaded .osm file.

Fictional partial export: one automatic match, one accepted match, and one new node; the remaining unreviewed stop is excluded. Never upload this demonstration data.

The button is disabled while work is in progress, before OSM retrieval, or when there are no exportable decisions. The application validates and saves the draft before initiating the browser download. A storage or validation failure must be resolved rather than treated as a successful export.

The overall progress indicator can differ from the export count because it also includes OSM-only items reviewed unchanged.

items.title: What the file contains
items.text:
The file can contain:

  • New nodes at GTFS coordinates, with profile-generated tags.
  • Selected existing nodes with their retained IDs and versions.
  • Selected platform ways with their retained IDs, versions, and member references.

The profile's geometry target controls matched-node coordinates. Way members are not moved by the GTFS geometry option. No element deletions are exported.

The file includes the default changeset metadata:

Key Default value comment Edit public transport features using GTFS data \| #Orcaboros host https://lumikeiju.dev/orcaboros/

Inspect and complete the changeset information in JOSM for the actual contribution. An error may use the generic phrase "OSM Change export"; that does not make the downloaded format an .osc file.

An export is an editing artifact, not a full session backup. Orcaboros does not import it to restore the review queue.

items.title: Conflicts that block export
items.text:
Two stops from the same feed cannot claim the same OSM element. Different feeds may share one element only when their geometry and tag decisions agree.

Export can therefore be blocked by:

  • Duplicate claims within one source feed.
  • Conflicting tags proposed for a shared OSM element.
  • Different required coordinates for a shared element.
  • Invalid coordinates, tags, element data, or inconsistent draft state.

Read the validation details. Where the interface links to affected review items, follow those links and reconcile the decisions. Verify which stop actually belongs to the element; do not create a duplicate node merely to bypass the conflict.

If correcting the profile is necessary, remember that applying it invalidates the existing candidates and reviews.

items.title: Inspect in JOSM
items.text:
Open the downloaded file in JOSM and inspect it against current OSM data before considering an upload.

  • Check for duplicate stops or platforms.
  • Check each changed or created object's position.
  • Verify names, mode-specific tagging, added stop codes, retained tags, and proposed removals.
  • Confirm that platform ways still have the intended members and geometry.
  • Resolve stale-data or upload conflicts using current OSM information.
  • Review JOSM's validation messages and the final upload summary.
  • Confirm the feed's permitted use, the applicable community process, and the actual changeset description.

No JOSM screenshot is included here: the illustrated workflow ends at Orcaboros's export controls. For JOSM's own interface, use the JOSM help.

Next: Sessions and troubleshooting.

items.title: Saved sessions
items.text:
Orcaboros stores its active session in the browser's IndexedDB. The stored data includes the profile, imported stops, OSM snapshot, review decisions, and export draft. Raw ZIP bytes are not retained.

Reopen the same application origin in the same browser profile to resume. Restoration rebuilds candidate evidence before exposing the saved reviews. There is no account or cloud synchronization, and a different browser, browser profile, or site origin has separate storage.

Do not treat browser storage as a durable backup. Keep the original archives and export useful profiles and .osm work separately. Those two export formats are not interchangeable, and neither restores an entire session.

The Overpass endpoint and custom style URL are not persisted. Re-enter them after a reload. Do not rely on theme choice or resized panel dimensions being restored either.

items.title: Operations that affect progress
items.text: Operation Effect Select replacement ZIP files Does not yet replace the active session Successfully process a new import Activates the newly imported session Fail or cancel an import Preserves the previous active session Apply a compatible profile change Reprocesses stops and invalidates candidates, reviews, and draft Successfully retrieve a fresh OSM snapshot Replaces candidates and invalidates earlier reviews and draft Fail or cancel retrieval Preserves the last successful snapshot and reviews Change a queue filter Changes visibility, not decisions or export eligibility Download an export Produces an editing file, not a session restore point Confirm session reset Clears the active imported/retrieved/reviewed work

items.title: Storage errors and multiple tabs
items.text:
If IndexedDB is entirely unavailable, the application can operate with memory-only storage. That work does not survive closing or reloading the page. A failure to save to an existing database is a separate problem: save errors are surfaced and should not be ignored.

When another tab changes the active session, Orcaboros can report:

The active session changed in another tab. Reload before continuing.

Continue in one tab and reload the stale one. Do not assume simultaneous tabs merge their decisions.

For a storage error, preserve any files already exported, check browser storage permissions and available space, and avoid clearing site data until you have decided to discard the saved session. Clearing site data is destructive, not a routine first troubleshooting step.

items.title: Reset the session
items.text:
1. Expand Upload.
  2. Select Reset current session.
  3. Choose Keep current session to cancel, or Reset session to confirm.

Confirmation clears imported data, candidates, reviews, and the active draft, along with the endpoint and custom style values. It is not an undo operation.

Resetting a session is also not the same control as Reset stock profile. Inspect the resulting profile rather than assuming session reset restores every profile default.

items.title: Layout and keyboard access
items.text:
• Use the header's Light mode / Dark mode button to switch appearance.
  • Use the skip-to-workspace link to bypass repeated header content.
  • Expand or collapse numbered workflow panels and the map legend as needed.
  • On wider screens, resize the sidebar and review area with their separators.
  • Focus a separator and use arrow keys for one-point adjustments, Shift+Arrow for five-point adjustments, or Home / End for its minimum/maximum.
  • The initial sidebar width is 25% of the viewport; the initial review area height is 46% of the viewport.
  • Narrow layouts stack the workspace vertically, so controls may be below the current view.
  • Escape cancels an active map-link change.

The application provides visible keyboard focus and reduced-motion support. Keep the textual state labels and legend in view rather than relying only on map colors.

items.title: Privacy and network access
items.text:
GTFS ZIP parsing and matching occur in the browser. Imported stops and the other session data are saved locally, rather than uploaded to an Orcaboros application backend.

Network activity is still part of using the hosted application:

  • The hosting service delivers the application and its resources.
  • The default or custom basemap loads external styles and map resources.
  • Starting retrieval sends a geographically bounded query to your selected Overpass endpoint, including the relevant feed-identity keys.

Do not interpret "local processing" as "no third-party requests." The deployed host may also load its own analytics resources. Endpoint and custom-style settings are session-only, but the services receiving requests still have their own privacy policies.

items.title: Common problems
items.text:
Symptom Checks and next steps A stock profile did not load Check the ZIP's editable feed ID against the stock table. One unknown ID causes a blank custom profile for all selected feeds. A feed ID is rejected Check hyphens, unsupported characters, duplicate IDs, length, and the prohibited US-WA-PSC ID. stops.txt cannot be found Check that it is the exact ZIP-root entry, not nested in another directory. Fewer stops were imported than expected Read diagnostics; check required values, coordinates, duplicate IDs, and unsupported location types. Profile import or editing fails Read the reported field/rule error. Check enabled feeds, radii, active key/value validity, and overlapping output keys. Reset stock profile fails for a custom feed Use a compatible custom profile; the stock registry cannot define that feed. Overpass retrieval fails Check HTTPS, endpoint availability, CORS, request size, timeouts, and the displayed error. A failed request is not an empty successful snapshot. No candidates were returned Check the imported extent, feed IDs, radius, and supported OSM types. Do not immediately create new nodes. The queue looks empty or too short Check category filters, especially exact, and pagination. Review progress exceeds the export count OSM-only unchanged items count toward progress; skipped/unreviewed stops do not export. An automatic match appeared in the export Auto-matched stops are eligible even when exact results are hidden. Inspect or change their decisions before exporting again. An item says removed Its identity is absent from all valid imported stop IDs, not confirmed physically removed. Skipped rows with valid IDs still count as present. Review it unchanged; no deletion is exported. A map feature cannot be selected as a candidate It may exist only in the basemap, not in the retrieved OSM snapshot. Points are missing at a broad map zoom Zoom to level 11 or above or use the focus controls. The map fails to initialize Check WebGL2/browser support and use Retry map. The queue remains available. Tags did not change to the displayed GTFS values The comparison is read-only; differing existing values normally stay. Check profile/default behavior and make final edits in JOSM. Download is disabled Finish retrieval, wait for current work, and confirm at least one eligible decision. Export reports a conflict Reconcile duplicate element claims, tags, or coordinates using the affected review items. No file appears after a valid export Check the browser's download UI and permissions, and distinguish a blocked download from an application validation/storage error. Work is missing after reopening Check browser profile/origin, cleared or unavailable storage, another tab replacing the session, and whether a new import/reset occurred.

If a problem persists, report it in the Orcaboros issue tracker. Include the app version, browser, exact visible error, and reproducible steps. Remove credentials, private endpoint/style URLs, and any feed data you cannot share.

Reference: Profile JSON. Return to: Orcaboros manual.

items.title: Profile JSON reference
items.text: Use Import profile JSON and Export profile JSON in the Profile editor to exchange configurations. A profile is data, not an executable script or an entire saved session.

items.title: Top-level fields
items.text:
Field Type Requirement schemaVersion Number Exactly 1 id String Nonempty profile identifier name String Nonempty display name version String Nonempty profile version sourceFeeds Array At least one source-feed definition, with unique IDs mappingRules Array Tag rules; an empty array is allowed candidateRadiusMeters Number Greater than 0 and at most 10,000 autoIdRadiusMeters Number Greater than 0, at most 10,000, and no greater than the candidate radius

The app's default radii are 50 m and 10 m, respectively. They are explicit fields in an exported schema-v1 profile.

items.title: Source-feed definitions
items.text:
Each entry in sourceFeeds describes one feed.

Field Type Meaning id String Feed identity, using the same normalization and restrictions as upload IDs displayName String Nonempty source name enabled Boolean Whether the feed is enabled; every currently imported feed must be enabled geometryTarget String "osm" or "gtfs"; defaults to "osm" when absent streetNameCleanup Boolean Whether to compute cleaned street names; defaults to true when absent metadata Object, optional String key/value metadata available to rules additionalTags Array, optional Tag rules applied within this feed removeKeys Array of strings, optional Existing OSM keys to remove; defaults to an empty array

US-WA-PSC is not a valid configured source. A profile containing other feed IDs does not become a stock profile merely because it was imported.

The geometry setting moves matched nodes only when it is "gtfs". Platform ways keep their member geometry, and new nodes always use feed coordinates.

items.title: Rule values and applicability
items.text:
Rules in mappingRules and per-feed additionalTags have:

  • key: the output OSM tag key.
  • value: one of the value objects below.
  • appliesTo: an optional restriction.
Value object Result { "kind": "constant", "value": "platform" } A literal value { "kind": "field", "field": "stop_name_expanded" } The value of an imported or computed field { "kind": "source-metadata", "key": "operator" } The named value from the source feed's metadata

Fields can name existing stops.txt headers, including stop_id, stop_code, stop_name, coordinates, location_type, and parent_station. Computed fields include:

Field Value stop_name_expanded The name after the feed's cleanup setting is applied source_feed_id The source's feed ID source_feed_name The source's display name

To restrict a rule, use either or both of these arrays:

{
    "sourceFeedIds": ["MANUAL-DEMO"],
    "locationKinds": ["platform"]
}

That object is the value of appliesTo. Supported location kinds are "platform" and "station". Without a restriction, the rule applies generally within its containing scope; an additionalTags rule still belongs to its own feed.

For example, this rule adds an operator value only to platforms in the named feed:

{
    "key": "operator",
    "value": { "kind": "source-metadata", "key": "operator" },
    "appliesTo": {
        "sourceFeedIds": ["MANUAL-DEMO"],
        "locationKinds": ["platform"]
    }
}

The feed must supply the corresponding string in its metadata for that rule to have a value.

Rules cannot contain executable code, template expressions, arbitrary query filters, or Overpass QL. Empty values are omitted. Active keys/values must pass validation, and overlapping output keys for the same feature are invalid.

items.title: Validation constraints
items.text:
• OSM keys must be nonempty and at most 255 characters. Resolved values are limited to 255 characters. Control characters and invalid Unicode text are rejected.
  • Field names must be nonempty, at most 255 characters, and contain no control characters. An unavailable field or metadata value resolves to an empty value and produces no tag.
  • A source-metadata rule's lookup key must contain 1-64 ASCII letters, digits, underscores, periods, colons, or hyphens.
  • Feed IDs in appliesTo.sourceFeedIds must exist in the profile. Within a feed's additionalTags, only that containing feed can be named.
  • An explicitly empty applicability array matches nothing; omit the restriction to apply generally.

Identity output keys have additional requirements. A rule for gtfs:stop_id:<FEED_ID> must:

  1. Name a feed configured in sourceFeeds.
  2. Use { "kind": "field", "field": "stop_id" } as its value.
  3. Apply only to that feed. In a multi-feed profile, set appliesTo.sourceFeedIds to an array containing exactly that feed ID.
  4. Apply to every location kind: omit appliesTo.locationKinds, even if the currently imported rows are all platforms.

For example:

{
    "key": "gtfs:stop_id:MANUAL-DEMO",
    "value": { "kind": "field", "field": "stop_id" },
    "appliesTo": { "sourceFeedIds": ["MANUAL-DEMO"] }
}

This rule is optional and is not part of the stock output mappings. If you deliberately add it, its active mapped value takes precedence over a removal rule for the same key.

items.title: Complete fictional example
items.text:
This is the profile used for the manual's fictional MANUAL-DEMO feed. It illustrates the schema, not approved tagging or data for a real import.

{
    "schemaVersion": 1,
    "id": "manual-demo",
    "name": "Fictional demonstration profile",
    "version": "1.0.0",
    "sourceFeeds": [
        {
            "id": "MANUAL-DEMO",
            "displayName": "Fictional manual examples",
            "enabled": true,
            "geometryTarget": "osm",
            "streetNameCleanup": true,
            "additionalTags": [
                {
                    "key": "public_transport",
                    "value": { "kind": "constant", "value": "platform" },
                    "appliesTo": { "locationKinds": ["platform"] }
                },
                {
                    "key": "highway",
                    "value": { "kind": "constant", "value": "bus_stop" },
                    "appliesTo": { "locationKinds": ["platform"] }
                }
            ],
            "removeKeys": ["gtfs:stop_id:MANUAL-DEMO"]
        }
    ],
    "mappingRules": [
        {
            "key": "name",
            "value": { "kind": "field", "field": "stop_name_expanded" }
        },
        {
            "key": "gtfs:stop_code:MANUAL-DEMO",
            "value": { "kind": "field", "field": "stop_code" }
        }
    ],
    "candidateRadiusMeters": 50,
    "autoIdRadiusMeters": 10
}

Here, stop_id helps identify a feature but is not an output mapping. The stop-code mapping is distinct from the identity key selected for removal. With multiple feeds, use appropriate feed restrictions and feed-specific tag keys rather than copying the example unchanged.

items.title: Validation and older files
items.text:
The editor omits blank/incomplete inactive rows when exporting JSON. Invalid active rules are reported before replacing the current profile or activating an import.

Older profiles missing geometryTarget, streetNameCleanup, or removeKeys receive the defaults described above. Legacy non-direct rules in mappingRules are migrated to the applicable feeds' additionalTags.

After importing, inspect the resulting feed sections and example outputs. Applying a compatible profile still invalidates candidates, reviews, and the draft, even when the file itself passes validation.

Return to: Mapping profiles or the Orcaboros manual.

items.title: Getting started
items.text: Tarralappu is a browser workspace for generating images through OpenRouter. You do not need to install Tarralappu to use the hosted application.

items.title: Before you begin
items.text:
Have a modern browser with JavaScript and browser storage enabled, an internet connection, and an OpenRouter account and API key. Check your account's available credits, model access, and provider-side spending limit before making paid requests.

The model catalogue can load without a key, and you can prepare drafts without generating. Generate, a draft's Refine button, Retry, and Random can send requests that use credits. A local session cap is useful for tracking, but it is not a guaranteed maximum charge.

items.title: Connect your key
items.text:
1. Select API Key in the header.
  2. Enter your OpenRouter API key in OpenRouter API key.
  3. Optionally select Remember on this device on a trusted personal device.
  4. Select Connect. The panel shows Key ✓ when a key is set.

Connecting stores the entered key; it does not verify that the account has credits or access to a particular model. A request can still fail because of authentication, account, model, or provider restrictions.

Without Remember on this device, the key is kept in memory and browser session storage. Remembering it also stores it in local storage, where JavaScript running on that page can access it. Avoid this option on shared devices. Change key clears the stored key and lets you enter another one.

Never put an API key in a prompt, screenshot, issue report, or shared request log. The key is not stored in the board's IndexedDB records or included in the request-source viewer.

items.title: Set a budget and inspect the workspace
items.text:
Expand Style & References. In Session cost cap ($), enter a positive amount and move focus out of the field to save it. A blank or nonpositive value removes the cap. Read How this cap works and the budget guide: unknown or underestimated requests can exceed a local cap.

The same panel contains the shared Style Guide, Style Reference, and Layout Reference. They are optional. Prompt Board is a separate shelf for reusable notes. The header displays the session total and Parallel job setting.

items.title: Create your first sketch
items.text:
1. Select New Sketch.
  2. Filter the model list if needed and select an image model. Review its displayed pricing and any capability warning.
  3. Optionally enter a prompt, then select Create Draft.
  4. In the new card, enter a nonempty Generation prompt if you did not already provide one.
  5. Review the attachment checkboxes and the model's available settings.
  6. When you are ready to make a paid request, select Generate.

Example model selection and prompt. Available models and prices can change.

Creating the draft does not start generation. A model is required to create it; a nonempty prompt is required to generate. The row stays associated with the selected model, so create another sketch or send a Prompt Board note to another model to compare.

Watch the card move through Queued and Generating to Done or Error. When the result is ready, open it with the magnifying-glass control or use its Download link. See Results and media before relying on a browser-stored image as your only copy.

Next: Prompts and shared style.

items.title: Prompts and shared style
items.text: Tarralappu separates a sketch's subject prompt from reusable board-level style guidance. You can write both yourself; generated suggestions are optional.

items.title: Write a Style Guide
items.text:
Expand Style & References and enter shared visual direction in Style Guide, for example, colors, lighting, texture, or medium. The text is saved as you edit.

A Style Guide is not automatically sent with every request. On a sketch, select Attach Style Description to include the current guide. New root drafts initially check this option when a guide is present; ordinary refinements start with shared attachments unchecked. Check the actual card before generating.

The guide can work alongside a Style Reference image and a Layout Reference image, but each attachment has its own checkbox. See References and markup.

items.title: Use the Prompt Board
items.text:
1. Expand Prompt Board and select Add Note.
  2. Optionally name the note and enter its prompt text. Edits save after a short pause.
  3. Use the note's copy control to copy the text, or Send to… to create drafts from it.
  4. Use the remove control to delete a note you no longer need.

Removing a note removes it from the board; it does not delete drafts previously created from it. A note can be blank while you work, but a nonempty prompt is needed for selection and sending.

Example notes are scratchpad content. Sending them creates drafts, not image requests.

items.title: Send to one or more models
items.text:
Use the send control on a note, or select the checkboxes on several nonempty notes and select Send to…. In the dialog:

  1. Filter the catalogue if useful and check the models to compare.
  2. Use the star controls to pin or unpin models without losing the selection.
  3. Confirm Send to or Create … drafts.

Each selected prompt/model combination creates a separate root draft. For example, two prompts and three models create six drafts. Inspect and generate each draft deliberately; the send action does not start image generation. If an error reports that some drafts may already have been created, check the board before repeating the action.

items.title: Random suggestions
items.text:
Random appears on the Style Guide, Prompt Board notes, and editable sketch prompts. It uses DeepSeek Flash through OpenRouter, not the sketch's image model. It needs a connected key, uses API credits, and replaces the target text rather than appending to it. On a note without a name, it can also supply a short name; an existing name is preserved.

Only one Random text request runs at a time. Cancel stops waiting for that request and leaves the existing text unchanged, but OpenRouter may still charge for processed tokens. A failed request also leaves the prior text in place; read the displayed error and cost status before retrying.

Random does not start image generation or change attachment selections. Existing board text and reference images are not sent as context for the Random request. Review the returned suggestion before using it.

Next: Models and generation.

items.title: Choose a model
items.text:
The New Sketch model picker loads OpenRouter's image-model catalogue and groups models by creator. Use Filter models… to narrow the list and the star beside a model to pin or unpin it. Pinned models appear first and remain available in their creator group. Pins are shared with the Prompt Board's Send to… dialog.

The picker displays available pricing and, where possible, a relative cost tier. Pricing not listed is not a promise that a model is free. Prices and capabilities can change; confirm current terms with OpenRouter before generating.

If the catalogue fails to load, use Retry. Some models are labelled capabilities estimated when detailed discovery is unavailable. Their controls use conservative defaults, not a guarantee of provider support. For GPT Image 2.6 Sunburst and Flare, Tarralappu checks endpoint details and blocks generation if it cannot confirm the endpoint; use Retry endpoint discovery when offered.

items.title: Configure a draft
items.text:
The controls on a draft depend on its model and discovered endpoint. You may see:

Control Purpose Aspect and Size Choose among the model's advertised aspect ratios and size options Quality and Background Select supported quality and background choices Outputs Request multiple images in one generation, up to the displayed model limit Format Choose an offered output format or the provider default Compression Set the allowed compression value for JPEG or WebP output Seed Supply a supported nonnegative seed, or leave it blank for random Reasoning Set reasoning effort when offered for the model Stream Show provider-supplied intermediate raster previews when supported

Outputs is the number of images in one request. It is not the fork count, and it is not the header's Parallel concurrency setting. Changing output count, quality, size, format, or references can change the charge.

For supported GPT Image 2.6 endpoints, Advanced image controls can expose Complexity, Moderation, custom Pixel size, GIF frame controls, or partial-preview count. Their presence depends on endpoint confirmation. Reset advanced options to provider defaults clears those advanced choices. The feature-availability disclosure explains controls that could not be confirmed; masks and SVG author selection are not offered.

The controls shown depend on the selected model and the endpoint's reported capabilities.

When custom still-image pixel sizing is available, use auto or WIDTHxHEIGHT. Both dimensions must be multiples of 16, neither edge may exceed 3840 pixels, the ratio must be between 1:3 and 3:1, and the total must be 655,360–8,294,400 pixels. Sizes above 2560 × 1440 are experimental. A custom size takes precedence over aspect and size options in the request.

items.title: Format and streaming restrictions
items.text:
• Compression applies to JPEG and WebP, not PNG or GIF.
  • If an explicit format is selected for a transparent background, use PNG or WebP.
  • GIF and multiple outputs use buffered completion rather than streaming. When a GPT Image 2.6 Sunburst or Flare endpoint offers SVG, that output also cannot stream, is generation-only, and requires one output.
  • For GPT Image 2.6, GIF frame controls and preview counts appear only when confirmed by the endpoint. GIF frame sizing is automatic; the offered frame count is within 2–16, and frame duration is within 20–2000 milliseconds in 10-millisecond increments, subject to narrower endpoint limits. The provider may return fewer previews than requested.
  • Streaming previews are temporary. Only completed output is saved, and an interrupted request can still be charged.

These are application constraints, not a promise that every listed format is available for every model. If an older saved selection is unavailable, choose an offered setting before generating. When switching from a custom still-image pixel size to GIF, reset the advanced options to clear the old size.

items.title: Start the request
items.text:
Review the prompt, selected references, output count, and budget. Select Generate on a root card or Refine on a refinement draft. A connected key, a nonempty prompt, compatible inputs, and available model capabilities are required.

Requests move through Queued and Generating to Done or Error. The header's Parallel setting controls how many image jobs can run at once. Creating a draft, selecting a model, and changing options do not start an image request.

The estimate can be unavailable or lower than the final cost. A local cap cannot prevent every overrun. See Costs and budgets before submitting requests.

Next: References and markup.

items.title: References and markup
items.text: References provide visual context for a request. They are distinct from the text in the Style Guide and from the prompt itself. The model may interpret them differently from what you intended, so inspect the result.

items.title: Shared style and layout images
items.text:
Expand Style & References and use the two slots under Reference Images:

Slot Intended guidance Style Reference Palette, texture, and mood Layout Reference Composition and placement

Use Upload style ref or Upload layout ref to choose a PNG, JPEG, or WebP file smaller than 50 MiB. The remove button beside an occupied slot removes that shared reference. To use it in a request, check Attach Style Reference or Attach Layout Reference on the sketch. The two checkboxes and Attach Style Description are independent.

New root drafts initially select shared context that is present when the draft is created. Ordinary new refinements start with those three attachments off. Check the flags on each card rather than assuming a reference is always sent. A conversational refinement may still include earlier context in its retained history.

Inputs count against the model's total image limit. The limit includes previous outputs, subject references, and checked global images. Tarralappu shows warnings when a model cannot accept images or the selected inputs do not fit. Upload validation and the upstream encoded-request limit are separate: an image accepted for storage can still be too large to send.

items.title: Subject references and the edit source
items.text:
For a supported dedicated image endpoint, expand Subject references and edit source on the editable card.

  1. Use Upload subject references to add PNG, JPEG, or WebP images smaller than 50 MiB each.
  2. Use Earlier and Later to change their order, or Remove to detach one.
  3. If editing an existing image, choose a Primary edit source from the previous outputs or subject references.
  4. Review the input count and any checked shared references before generating.

The example selects the previous result as the primary edit source and keeps a separate subject reference.

The chosen edit source is sent first; other subject references follow in their selected order, then checked shared reference images. Choosing a source does not automatically remove the other subject references. With Use previous outputs in order (legacy), previous outputs are used in order instead of selecting one primary source.

Changing the primary source clears any saved markup tied to the old source. Removing the selected subject source also clears its markup. Set the source first, then prepare annotations.

items.title: Use GIF or SVG results as edit inputs
items.text:
Edit inputs must be raster PNG, JPEG, or WebP. Generated GIF and SVG files remain available in their original formats, but they must be explicitly converted before use as an edit source.

In the refinement's Previous output disclosure, choose Use first frame as PNG for a GIF or Rasterize to PNG reference for an SVG. This creates a separate PNG subject reference, selects it as the primary source, and leaves the original unchanged. Check the resulting reference and output settings before sending the edit.

items.title: Markup-guided edits
items.text:
Markup-guided edit is available only when the selected endpoint confirms markup support. It uses a separate transparent PNG overlay aligned with the selected raster source; it is guidance for the model, not an exact mask.

  1. Select a primary PNG, JPEG, or WebP edit source.
  2. Open Markup-guided edit and select Add annotation.
  3. Choose a circle, rectangle, or arrow, then enter its x, y, width, and height values in image pixels. Keep the shape within the source bounds.
  4. Use Undo, Redo, or Clear annotations as needed, then select Save transparent markup.
  5. In the prompt, describe the desired change and what should remain unchanged.

Alternatively, use Upload matching transparent PNG. It must be smaller than 50 MiB, match the oriented source dimensions, and contain transparent pixels. The markup and its base may contain at most 16,777,216 pixels. Remove saved markup detaches the overlay. If support is not confirmed or endpoint discovery fails, follow the displayed message rather than assuming markup will be sent.

Next: Chains and forks.

items.title: Chains and forks
items.text: A chain is a horizontal row of sketches using the same model. Each completed sketch can produce media; an editable draft records the next request before it is sent.

items.title: Continue a chain
items.text:
1. Wait until the latest card in the row is Done.
  2. Select the ghost + Refine card at the end of the row.
  3. Enter a Refinement prompt describing the change.
  4. Review the inherited settings, previous output, references, and local caps.
  5. Select the draft's Refine button when ready to submit.

The second card is an editable draft; creating it does not send the refinement.

The + Refine card adds a draft only after the latest sketch is complete. It inherits generation settings and starts with an empty prompt. Shared Style Guide and global-image attachments start unchecked; inspect them if you want to send them again. If a parent has multiple outputs, the edit-source controls can select a particular output when supported.

An image-only model uses image-to-image for refinements rather than conversational history. Conversational models can include earlier prompts and images, subject to input limits; older context may be truncated to fit. Neither approach guarantees that the model will preserve every detail.

items.title: Create alternative rows
items.text:
Use the count selector and fork controls on a card to create 1–10 independent draft rows. The available action depends on the card:

Action Available from What it creates Initial-run fork A root draft or errored root A new root draft with the model, prompt, and settings copied Re-run fork A completed card A new draft for that prompt, with the completed path before it copied when applicable Refinement fork A completed card, or an editable/errored refinement A new row with a copied completed path and an editable refinement draft

Forks are drafts, not automatic generation requests. They keep the source row's model. Copied completed images are reused without a new generation charge, while each eventual new request can cost money. A new fork has no chain cap until you set one; the session cap still applies.

Use + Refine to continue the existing row. Use a refinement fork to explore alternatives in separate rows. A forked refinement carries a copied prompt and settings, so review them rather than assuming it is blank.

items.title: Retry, delete, or cancel
items.text:
An Error card shows the problem and offers Retry. Retrying sends another request; check the error, settings, and any known or unreported charges first.

The trash control marks that card and all later cards in its row for deletion. Review the displayed count, then choose Delete … cards or Cancel. Deleting the first card removes the row. This is also the way to cancel a queued or generating image job: confirm deletion of that card. There is no separate image-generation cancel button.

Deletion is not an undoable backup. Download anything you need first. Other forked rows retain their own references to shared images, but deleting a card removes its image-generation charge from the local total. Cancellation or an interrupted request can still incur an OpenRouter charge.

Next: Results and media.

items.title: Inspect and download
items.text:
A Done card shows its prompt and each returned image. Expand the prompt summary to read the full text. Select a result's magnifying-glass control to open Image viewer; close it with the close button, Escape, or the backdrop.

Example output in the image viewer. The generated image is illustrative, not a promise of a particular result.

Use Download PNG, Download JPEG, Download WEBP, Download GIF, or Download SVG, as offered for the returned file. Tarralappu downloads the original stored media rather than a screenshot of the preview. Save important files outside the browser.

The card reports the number of outputs received and, where available, dimensions, format, animation metadata, provider settings, and known cost. The provider may return different metadata or fewer outputs than requested; read any warning on the card.

items.title: Animation and vector output
items.text:
An animated GIF initially shows a still poster. Use Play animation to play it and Pause animation to stop. The original GIF download remains animated. Frame count and duration are displayed when available.

SVG results are displayed as images rather than inserted as page markup. If a later edit needs a GIF or SVG as its input, explicitly create a PNG still or raster reference first; the original download is not replaced. See References and markup.

items.title: Add an image description
items.text:
Open Image description beneath a result or reference and enter a description of the visible content. Move focus out of the field to save it. The description can contain up to 500 characters and is used as the image's alternative text in Tarralappu. Clearing the field removes the saved description.

Descriptions are stored with the browser's image record. They are not a substitute for describing an image where you publish it, and they are not embedded into the original download by this control.

items.title: Inspect the request
items.text:
On a completed card or a card with a recorded request, select View request source (</>). The panel shows the recorded request shape and offers Copy. Image data is elided and the key is not included, but the source can still contain prompts and other information you may not want to share.

An error card may separately offer View raw response. Treat raw responses as potentially sensitive: review and redact them before sharing. Neither panel is a complete backup of the board or image files.

Next: Costs and budgets.

items.title: Costs and budgets
items.text:
Image generation and Random text generation use OpenRouter. Review current model pricing, account access, and provider billing information before sending requests.

Local caps are not hard billing limits

Estimates can be unavailable or lower than the final charge. Requests with unknown estimates can exceed a local cap, and interrupted or failed requests may still be billed. Set an OpenRouter spending limit for provider-enforced protection and check OpenRouter for the authoritative charges.

items.title: Read costs
items.text:
The header's Session total includes known image-generation charges on retained sketch cards and known Random text costs. A chain header shows that row's known total; a completed card can show its known charge. The Incomplete indicator or an unreported-cost warning means some charges may be missing.

The model picker may show price components and approximate $ tiers. Those tiers are rough hints across different billing schemes, not exact request quotes. An unavailable estimate or pricing not listed does not mean zero cost.

Tarralappu records reported cost when available and may look up a generation's usage afterward. Known charges from repeated attempts are accumulated. An error, cancellation, lost response, or storage problem can leave a charge unknown, so compare against OpenRouter rather than treating the local total as a bill.

items.title: Set local caps
items.text:
• Session cost cap ($): expand Style & References, enter a positive amount, and leave the field to save it. This covers the board's known image and Random text costs.
  • Chain cost cap: enter a positive amount in the Cap $ field at the right of that row's header and leave the field to save it. It applies to image requests in that chain.
  • Clear a cap by leaving its field blank or entering a nonpositive value.

The app includes known in-flight estimates when checking budgets. It blocks a request if a cap is already reached, or if a known estimate would exceed the relevant cap. An unknown estimate is not zero: the request can proceed while the cap has room and still cost more than the remaining amount. Random uses the session cap, not a chain cap.

A new fork starts without a chain cap; set one on the new row if desired. Copied history in a fork does not represent a new request or charge. Deleting a sketch removes its image-generation cost from local totals, while Random text costs remain. These totals therefore do not necessarily equal your complete provider account history.

items.title: Parallel jobs
items.text:
The header's Parallel control sets image-job concurrency; the interface offers values from 1 to 8, with 2 as the initial default. It does not change the number of outputs in a single request or the number of forks. Multiple jobs may be in flight, so known estimates are reserved when checking caps.

Random text uses its own one-at-a-time guard. Starting or cancelling Random does not start or cancel an image-generation job.

Next: Storage and troubleshooting.

items.title: What is saved
items.text:
Tarralappu saves its board, prompts, model pins, sketch chains, settings, image records, and available cost information in the browser's IndexedDB. Reopen the same application origin in the same browser profile to use that stored board.

The API key is separate: by default it is held in memory and session storage; Remember on this device opts into local storage. Neither the board database nor a request-source snapshot contains the key.

Browser storage can be cleared, evicted, unavailable, or tied to a different browser profile or origin. There is no account-based board synchronization or full-board backup/export control in v2.1.0. Download important images and keep copies of important prompt text separately. An individual image download does not restore a chain, its settings, or its history.

If the page is closed or reloaded while a sketch is queued or generating, the card is restored as an Error and can be retried. A request interrupted after it started may still have been charged. Check OpenRouter before retrying.

items.title: Privacy and network access
items.text:
The application has no Tarralappu backend. Model discovery and generation use network requests to OpenRouter; the selected model provider may process the prompt and images included in a request. Hosting the application and any provider service are separate from local board storage.

Only send material you are allowed to share. Be especially careful with private reference images, prompts, raw errors, and copied request source. The Random text requests do not send your existing board text or reference images, but they still use OpenRouter and can cost credits.

items.title: Layout and keyboard access
items.text:
• Use Skip to main content to bypass the header.
  • Expand or collapse Style & References and Prompt Board to make room for the board.
  • Rows extend horizontally; scroll the row to reach later sketches and the + Refine card.
  • Use the header's theme button to switch between light and dark.
  • Reference-order buttons, annotation fields, dialogs, and card actions are keyboard accessible. Escape closes the image viewer.

items.title: Common problems
items.text:
Symptom Checks and next steps Saved data will not load Check browser storage permissions and available space, then select Try again. Avoid clearing site data unless you intend to discard the board. The model list is empty or fails Check the connection, clear the filter, and use Retry. Catalogue and endpoint availability can change. A model or option is missing Check the selected model and endpoint. Some capabilities are estimated or require endpoint confirmation; use the offered discovery retry. A draft cannot generate Enter a prompt, connect a key, and check model capabilities, endpoint errors, input limits, and incompatible options. The key is set but a request fails Check the displayed error, OpenRouter account access, credits, and model availability. Connect alone does not validate the key. A reference cannot be uploaded or sent Use PNG, JPEG, or WebP; check file and model input limits. A file can pass upload validation but exceed the encoded request limit. A GIF or SVG cannot be used for an edit Convert the previous output to a PNG reference explicitly; retain the original download. Markup is unavailable or rejected Confirm endpoint support, choose a primary raster source, and use a transparent PNG matching its dimensions. A request is blocked by a cap Check both the session and chain cap, including other known in-flight estimates. Do not treat unknown estimates as free. A card is interrupted or fails Read the error and any known or unreported charge. Correct the cause and retry only after checking possible provider charges. The local total seems too low Deleted sketches no longer contribute their image charges; some costs can be unreported. Check OpenRouter for the complete bill. Expected work is missing Check the browser profile and application origin, whether site data was cleared, and whether the card or its ancestor was deleted.

If a problem persists, use the Tarralappu issue tracker. Include the app version, browser, visible error, and reproducible steps. Remove API keys, private prompts, images, and sensitive response details before sharing.
